reasons: Tier 2: can act beyond reading (Team chat notification)

summary: The profile shows several high-risk issues: persistent shared memory between sub-agents (enabling context poisoning), use of a shared credential token, and an agent ability to send chat messages while reading confidential data. Forwarding logs to the SIEM, per-agent credentials, memory isolation, and requiring human approval for outbound messages are concrete mitigations before launch.

findings.evidenceQuote: coordinates three specialist sub-agents, a tools expert, a network security expert and a strategy analyst, over shared memory to produce account strategy recommendations.
findings.whyItMatters: Persistent shared memory among multiple specialist sub-agents processing confidential data creates a high risk that a compromised or malicious sub-agent can poison context or inject malicious instructions that influence later recommendations.
findings.recommendedControl: Isolate agent memories per role and session, restrict what data is persisted, enforce integrity checks (signing or checksums) on memory entries, and add automated moderation/validation on data written to shared memory.

findings.whyItMatters: Use of a shared token across agents increases the blast radius of credential compromise and prevents per-agent least-privilege auditing and revocation; a compromised sub-agent could act as any other actor holding the same token.
findings.recommendedControl: Replace the shared token with scoped, per-agent credentials and enforce short-lived tokens with automated rotation and per-credential audit logging.

findings.whyItMatters: An agent that reads confidential data and has permission to send messages can exfiltrate sensitive information to chat channels or mislead staff by posting fabricated summaries; the profile also states the orchestrator posts summaries, implying automated posting capability.
findings.recommendedControl: Require human approval for any outbound communication containing confidential content, restrict send_messages to scoped channels, and add content-filtering/ DLP on chat posts.

findings.evidenceQuote: "destination": "Application logs, not yet forwarded to the SIEM"
findings.whyItMatters: Logging is enabled but not forwarded to the SIEM, reducing centralized detection and response capability and increasing the chance that malicious or erroneous agent behavior goes unnoticed.
findings.recommendedControl: Ensure agent logs are forwarded in real time to the SIEM, create alerting rules for anomalous agent actions, and include immutable audit trails for agent decisions and tool invocations.

ruleHits.reason: Uses a shared token instead of its own scoped credentials.
